name: Motorcycle
description: A motor-driven vehicle with a seat or saddle, designed to travel on no more than three wheels, at any power; the registration law adds a top speed over 50 mph, below which a step-through one is a motor scooter. A plug-in battery-powered one is an electric motorcycle.

restrictions.rule: A seat or saddle, and no more than three wheels on the ground
The traffic law sets no power or speed floor, so one whose motor produces no more than 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W) is still a motorcycle; Kentucky has no separate motor-driven cycle class
For registration, a top speed over 50 mph; a slower step-through one of 2 brake horsepower or more is a motor scooter, registered as a motorcycle

Kentucky's moped definition is written around an engine of 50 cc or less with no electric equivalent, so an electric moped-class vehicle isn't a moped; the traffic law makes it a motorcycle, though at 50 mph or less it fits no registration class
Riders need a motorcycle operator's license, and must use approved eye protection
Riders and passengers under 21, permit holders and riders licensed less than a year must wear an approved helmet
A rider on an instruction permit may not carry passengers
Titled and registered, and must carry insurance; a plug-in battery-powered one pays an annual electric motorcycle fee at registration
